text.aria-label: Title text 'The ERA5-trained model loses to the ENS-trained model without lags, and training on recent years only closes most of the gap'

g.text: The ERA5-trained model loses to the ENS-trained model without lags, and training on recent years only closes most of the gap

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Change in mean absolute error (points of capacity; more negative means the first model is better), by how many days ahead the forecast is. ERA5: ECMWF's estimate of past weather. ENS: ECMWF's 51-member ensemble weather forecast; every forecast is the mean over the 51 members. Every model is an XGBoost model. 22 electricity series (16 primary-substation demand, 4 bulk or grid supply flows, 2 battery or biofuel); 73 ENS runs, one every 5 days, July 2025 to June 2026. Intervals come from re-drawing whole months at random and fitting with different random seeds. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval. Solid rule: no difference.'
text.tspan: Change in mean absolute error (points of capacity; more negative means the first model is better), by how many days ahead the forecast is.
ERA5: ECMWF's estimate of past weather. ENS: ECMWF's 51-member ensemble weather forecast; every forecast is the mean over the 51 members. Every model is an XGBoost model.

22 electricity series (16 primary-substation demand, 4 bulk or grid supply flows, 2 battery or biofuel); 73 ENS runs, one every 5 days, July 2025 to June 2026. Intervals come from re-drawing whole months at random and fitting with different random seeds.
Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval. Solid rule: no difference.
